answer: A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The timber multiplier is published, charged in violet, and kernel lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 7 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 3420 identities would post 1823 proofs and burn roughly 88 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
